newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end off on fund liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end off on fund liquidation.

text.p: CME live cattle futures ended lower on continued fund liquidation prompted by weak technical and fundamental factors. Feeder cattle fell sharply on technical sell stops, traders said.
Live cattle ended 0.325 to 0.075 cent lower with April off 0.350 at 65.275 cents. Feeder cattle finished 0.825 to 0.100 lower with March off 0.675 at 67.350 cents.
Live cattle fell to 7-week lows and feeders to 5-week lows on the setback.
Fund liquidation added to weakness in cash beef to press live cattle futures, traders said.
"The (futures) market got through moving averages and funds were exiting," one trader said.

Trading was slow early in live cattle awaiting developments in the cash fed cattle market, but fundamental pressure developed on the weak undertone to cash beef and expectations that packers will not raise their bids for cash cattle. Packers appear to have adequate live supplies to meet kill needs into the week and beef will have to firm before packers will boost their bids, traders said.
Back months paced the decline in further technical weakness as charts pointed down since highs posted last week.

Feeders also showed carryover technical pressure and sell stops took prices down to new lows. Futures turned technically weak last week after setting new contract highs and then falling the rest of the week, chartists said.

A weak tone to cash feeders also weighed on the market. The USDA reported cash feeders under pressure at Oklahoma City as expected. Other feeder markets were also showing a weak undertone due to slow demand, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.01 at $70.29 per cwt.

Cargill Investor Services and E.D.&F. Man sold April while RBH and ADM Investor Services bought. Refco bought February while spreaders sold. Cargill and E.D.&F. Man sold March feeders while LFG bought. RBH notably sold April on the setback earlier, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, trading was active late with commercials buying April 68 and 70 calls. There was continued hedging in June, buying puts and selling calls, pit sources added.
